messages:
maria: Heads-up — after enabling prefill+speculative on the new 14b-quant variant we see a small but reproducible quality regression: ~0.45% of completions contain stale prefix tokens (repeat of earlier context) instead of continuing the prompt. Not sure if this is prefetch KV staleness or a rollout bug. cc @rian :thinking_face:

rian: ugh. can you paste a short reproducible sample + the request id? also which fallback path did you enable (fp16 -> q4_0? q4_1?)

maria: sample below (redacted). request_id: req-2026-03-21-8a7c

```
PROMPT: 
User: Summarize the following conversation about deployment timings.
Context: [Conversation chunk A that ended with "we'll ship Wed"]
Model output (bad): 
... we'll ship Wed ... we'll ship Wed ... then the rest of unrelated content

LOG (trim): prefetch:start req=req-2026-03-21-8a7c model=redwood-14b-quant prefetch_variant=q4_0 fallback_path=fp16->q4_0 kv_hit=1 kv_version=42
kv_apply: looked-up prefix_id=abc123 last_used=2026-03-20T23:12:02Z
serve: response returned 200 latency=84ms
```

devon: that log smells like a cached prefix from a previous request returned even though the model variant changed. two hypotheses: (1) prefix_id collision because we compute prefix key without including quant variant in the hash, or (2) async prefetch completed with stale token offsets and applied to current state.

jess_qa: I can repro locally with the 14b-quant image and a small harness. steps i used: run 1000 random prompts with prefill enabled + randomized session ids, compare ngram overlap to prior run without prefill; saw 0.4% overlap where prefix repeats.

maria: good. @devon can you confirm how prefix ids are generated? we should have included model variant and sequence_id in the key, but code path might be using the canonical prompt hash only.
devon: looking now. in prefetch/keygen.cc the key concat is: `sha256(prompt || user_id)` — yep, no model_variant. that's our bug for sure. quick patch: include `model_variant` and `seq_offset` in the hash.

rian: nice catch. are there performance risks? adding variant to key means cache misses after rollouts which is okay. main risk: KV explosion if we create many keys for the same prompt across tiny variant diffs. but better consistency.

maria: agreed — safer to avoid correctness regressions. plan proposal:
- patch keygen to include `model_variant` (and `quant_tag`), add a feature flag `prefetch_strict_keys`
- rollout to canary (1% traffic) for 24h, run the QA harness and our eval set (N=50k prompts)
- add instrumentation: emit `cache_key_components` in prefetch debug logs for a sample of requests

jess_qa: I'll run the harness in prod-shadow mode against canary and baseline. can also add an automated check: if prefix_repeat_rate > 0.2% fail the rollout.

ops-bot: deploy request created: deploy/5523456795 -> staging -> canary(1%). Owner: devon. ETA: 45m. :robot_face:

devon: patch created, unit tests added for key composition, running CI now. quick note: need a migration for existing cache entries? we can let them expire naturally; the new keys will just miss and repopulate.

rian: sounds good. one more thought: add a debug-only `key_echo` header so customers can opt-in to assert key differences during onboarding. helps root-cause if they see quality drift when we change variants.

maria: perfect. I'll post a short runbook with mitigation steps (disable prefetch / disable speculative on the route) and link the canary dashboards. thanks all :eyes:

jess_qa: will report back with numbers from the canary run in ~6h.

devon: CI green; shipping to staging now.

maria: thanks — closing the loop after canary.
